newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent crude trades higher on U.S stocks data.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent crude trades higher on U.S stocks data.

text.p: SIMEX Brent crude rebounded at midday on Wednesday from its previous close in London, tracking ACCESS trade after the release of new stocks figures, brokers said.
June was last traded at $18.13 per barrel, rising 14 cents from its last IPE close at $17.99.
"The gains were on the back of bullish API figures," a broker said.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) figures showed a fall in distillates stock of 4.7 million barrels to 96.3 million last week. Gasoline stocks dropped 1.9 million to 195 million.
On ACCESS, June was last traded at $19.71, up 12 cents from its last official close.

Brokers said the market has already discounted news of Shell's Nigeria declaration of force majeure of Bonny Light crude oil and Iraq sending helicopters to pick up Moslem pilgrims from the Saudi border despite U.S. warnings.

They said the news headlines had lent some support earlier on trades on IPE and NYMEX. But the bullish support tapered off later in the day when profit taking ahead of May expiry dominated trades, causing levels on both NYMEX and IPE to fall.
